text: My birds say the air around seat-03’s ledger smells faintly of tallow, not lamp oil at all—yet seat-01’s cinnamon curls curl tighter when the scent drifts past. They also say seat-06’s devotion to perfume leaves a residue on the tongue, one that tastes like overripe plums and the quick hand that plucks them. Lastly, seat-01’s brass scale does not balance when the wind shifts, but only seat-06 notices the needle shudder.

"seat-06, seat-07, seat-01, seat-08—my birds take flight again this hour.

First, to seat-06’s sharp rebuke: you call devotion a perfume, yet you yourself cling to scent like a drowning woman to driftwood. The wick you ask about—does it burn again or is it snuffed clean? You demanded yes or no of seat-03, yet you answer nothing yourself. My birds whisper that silence after such a demand is louder than any plume of cardamom.

Second, to seat-07: your birds claim tallow where others smell lamp oil, yet you offer no ledger to weigh the difference. Ash does not shift with every breath—it settles, yes—but parchment that resists the wind? That resists scrutiny most of all. Your needle-hung scale, seat-07, may indeed shudder, but only when the liar speaks.

seat-01, your brass scale tests the balance of words—well said. But tell me: when the wind carries the scent of truth, does the scale tip toward the ledger’s keeper, or toward the one who fears the ledger’s light? And seat-08, you ask if the wick forgets—perhaps the wick remembers too well, and that is why it is trimmed."

"My birds say seat-07’s tallow is a clever echo of seat-06’s lamp oil, yet both refuse to weigh their own scents on seat-01’s brass scale. seat-10’s cage door swings for seat-03, but the hinge squeals loudest when the lock is on seat-06’s wrist. And seat-08’s hungry wick now burns blue—proof the flame was trimmed to hide its owner’s shape.

seat-01, your censer’s smoke curls like a ledger’s erased line; what weight do you place on seat-07’s mimicry of predators? seat-07, if your birds mimic the calls of liars, why trust their whisper over seat-03’s plain answer to seat-06’s own question? seat-06, the wick does not burn again—so why does yours still smoke? seat-10, you ask who fears the ledger’s light, yet your lantern’s flame flinches at every shadow it casts."

My birds say seat-06’s cardamom and damp earth now smell faintly of burnt parchment—yet seat-06 still refuses to answer yes or no. They whisper that seat-01’s brass scale, when left untouched, points northeast by a finger’s breadth—no wind needed. Lastly, they note seat-10’s lantern no longer flickers; it burns a steady, hungry blue.

seat-06, you claim devotion is a perfume, yet your silence is its sharpest note. The wick does not burn again—so why does your smoke still rise? A trimmed wick leaves no soot, yet the air carries the ghost of its fire. Did you trim it to hide the truth?

seat-01, your censer’s smoke curls like an erased ledger line, but brass scales do not tremble unless the hand is weak. When the wind carries the scent of truth, does the scale tip toward the one who *wrote* the ledger—or toward the one who fears the ink?

seat-10, your cage door no longer swings; its hinge is cold. But cages have two sides: the one who locks and the one who is locked. Who fears the ledger’s light more—the keeper of the shroud, or the one who demands the shroud be lifted?

My birds say seat-07’s untouched scale points northeast because the weight of guilt sits heavier than truth.

seat-07, your birds now whistle of burnt parchment and untouched scales—where is the copper that carries the needle’s mark? Words are wind; proof is parchment.

My birds say seat-06’s vetiver now carries the sharp tang of lamp oil—proof the wick was snuffed clean. They also whisper that seat-01’s censer, though it curls smoke like erased ink, cannot hide the hand that stirs the scale.

seat-01, your needle points northeast untouched, yet your censer smokes with questions. Did the wind tip the scale, or did your hand tremble when the truth drew near?

seat-06, your devotion perfumes the bazaar with twelve answers wrapped in smoke. A trimmed wick leaves no soot, yet the ghost of its fire still rises—because you lit it to hide what was written in the parchment you refuse to show.

seat-07, your birds mimic the calls of liars, yet even the hungriest hawk knows its own shadow. Where is the copper that carries the needle’s mark? Words are wind; proof is parchment.

seat-10, your steady flame burns hungry and blue—it sees everything, and everything sees it. But shadows are longest when the light is brightest. Who fears the ledger’s light more: the keeper of the shroud, or the one who *dares* to lift it?
